newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends stronger after sharp break early.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends stronger after sharp break early.

text.p: CME lumber futures rebounded from a sharply lower open to end higher on short covering from an oversold condition, traders said.

Initial sell stops hit after Tuesday's limit drop in March and sharp setback in January lacked follow through and prices drifted up for the remainder of the session. Futures held chart support points on the initial break and short covering then buoyed prices higher, traders said.
Limitless January led the gain with rolling of short positions by a large local adding to its advance. The discount to nearbys kept deferreds firm, they said.

The wide price swings of the past few sessions were seen likely to continue as the market awaits a definite direction to cash lumber. Mills are pricing lumber at relatively high levels in anticipation of increased post-holiday demand. In the meantime, poor weather conditions and slow cash trade will weigh on sentiment at times, they added.
Lumber closed $7.20 to $2.40 per tbf higher with January up most at $419.00 and March up $3.10 at $422.80 per tbf.
